title: Cross-Framework Model Portability for Retail Analytics
business: Retail enterprises managing diverse machine learning infrastructure across different cloud and on-premise environments.
problem: Teams are siloed by framework choice, leading to redundant development of identical model architectures for PyTorch-based research and TensorFlow-based production environments, increasing technical debt and maintenance costs.
solution: Keras 3 enables developers to write a single model definition using backend-agnostic APIs, allowing the same codebase to run seamlessly on JAX, TensorFlow, or PyTorch backends without modification.
steps: Define the model architecture using only built-in Keras layers or the keras.ops namespace.
Configure the environment variable KERAS_BACKEND to target the desired framework (e.g., 'torch', 'tensorflow', or 'jax').
Utilize the standard Keras fit() or predict() routines which accept data from any source, including PyTorch DataLoaders or tf.data.Dataset.
Save the model in the framework-agnostic .keras format for deployment across different backend environments.
outcome: Unified model development lifecycle that eliminates framework-specific code duplication and ensures consistent model logic across heterogeneous deployment environments.
limitation: While logic is portable, random number generator behavior and floating-point implementations differ across backends, which can lead to minor numerical divergence over long training runs. Verify consistency by comparing output precision across backends.

diagram.title: Cross-Framework Model Deployment Flow
diagram.description: Shows how a single Keras definition targets multiple backends.

code.content:
import os
os.environ['KERAS_BACKEND'] = 'torch' # Switch backend to PyTorch
import keras
from keras import layers

# Define model once using backend-agnostic layers
model = keras.Sequential([layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'), layers.Dense(10)])

# Compile and train using standard Keras API
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mse')
# model.fit(data_loader) # Works with PyTorch DataLoader
code.explanation: Demonstrates setting the backend environment variable to PyTorch and using standard Keras layers that function regardless of the underlying framework.

questions.question: In Cross-Framework Model Portability for Retail Analytics, how does Keras 3 address the problem of siloed development?
options: By forcing all teams to migrate to a single proprietary framework.
By enabling developers to write a single model definition that runs on JAX, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
By providing a cloud-based service that automatically converts PyTorch code to TensorFlow.
By requiring separate codebases for every framework to ensure maximum performance.
questions.explanation: The solution explicitly states that Keras 3 allows developers to write a single model definition using backend-agnostic APIs for use across different frameworks.
questions.evidence: Keras 3 enables developers to write a single model definition using backend-agnostic APIs, allowing the same codebase to run seamlessly on JAX, TensorFlow, or PyTorch backends without modification.

questions.question: In Cross-Framework Model Portability for Retail Analytics, what is a key limitation of using Keras 3 across different backends?
options: The model cannot be saved in a framework-agnostic format.
The training loop must be rewritten for every backend.
Numerical divergence may occur due to differences in RNG and floating-point implementations.
Keras 3 only supports the TensorFlow backend for production serving.
questions.explanation: The limitation section highlights that while logic is portable, numerical differences can arise due to backend-specific RNG and floating-point behaviors.
questions.evidence: While logic is portable, random number generator behavior and floating-point implementations differ across backends, which can lead to minor numerical divergence over long training runs.
